clue.text: Be informed, as should an orchestral musician?

definitions.meaning: to be aware of how things really stand in a situation
a player must be familiar with the written music, the full printed part for the orchestra

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to stay up to date, just as a player in an orchestra must keep up with the music.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to understand the true facts of a situation, which is what being informed amounts to.

clue.text: Innings one short — foul play

parts.note: a knock is a batter's innings in cricket

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A batter's innings is cut short by unfair play.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby this is the offence of dropping or propelling the ball forwards with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a rugby infringement, so an instance of foul play on the field.

clue.text: Centre in form, a politician demonstrating eloquence

indicators.note: centre in takes the middle letters of the word that follows

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A politician in good form shows off his gift for speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of public speaking, delivered fluently and persuasively, is eloquence.

clue.text: So front is lower than that place

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece lower than another comes after it

parts.note: there means at that place
fore means the front, as in to the fore

explanation.surface: A spatial statement that the front sits lower than some other spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are connectives meaning as a consequence, introducing a conclusion.

clue.text: Bring joy to people ultimately, pushing up the daisies

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of the word is taken

parts.note: the idiom means dead and buried, as late does in the late king

explanation.surface: Cheering everyone up in the end, even though they are long dead.
explanation.definitionFit: To delight or thrill someone is to make them happy, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Hurtful piece taken from newspaper

definitions.meaning: wounding, as a sharp remark is
an article clipped out of a paper and kept

explanation.surface: A wounding article lifted from a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp unkind remark is wounding, and a press clipping is snipped out of the paper.

clue.text: After unfortunate arrest, time to begin afresh

indicators.note: after puts the letter for time at the end
unfortunate suggests things went wrong, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: After an unlucky arrest, someone decides it is time for a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To start again from the beginning is to begin afresh.

clue.text: Judg/ment?

parts.note: a verdict word cut in two by the slash is literally a judgement that has been divided

explanation.surface: A single word chopped by a slash, posed as a question.
explanation.walkthrough: In boxing, a fight decided by judges who do not all agree is given this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling on which the judges are divided is a judgement literally split, as the slash shows.

clue.text: Zero call for an end to change, finally

parts.note: zero is the figure 0, read as the letter O

indicators.note: to change means to alter, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: No one calls for an end to change, at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning conclusively and for the last time, it matches finally in the sense of definitively.

clue.text: Fuel for glass

parts.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: A puzzling note about fuel needed for making glass in a furnace.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas burned for heating and cooking, sold in bottles, is a common fuel.

clue.text: Skilled worker from Hobart is annoying

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A tradesman from the Tasmanian capital Hobart is irritating people.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who works skilfully with their hands is a classic skilled worker.

clue.text: Smokier bombs, irritating

indicators.note: bombs here means explodes or blows apart, so the letters of the word before are scattered

explanation.surface: Bombs that give off more smoke are a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiresome and annoying is a synonym for irritating.

clue.text: Islamic office I consider to be behind me, contrarily

indicators.note: the following pieces come after the turned word
contrarily means the other way round, so the short word is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
to rate something is to consider or judge it

explanation.surface: Someone reflects on a Muslim post they hold, judging it from the opposite viewpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or rank of an emir, a Muslim ruler, is a fair reading of Islamic office.

clue.text: Fine, daily limits?

wordplay.reading: D, Y: the limits of daily

parts.note: the limits of the word daily are its first letter D and last letter Y

explanation.surface: A question whether some daily allowance is acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old-fashioned adjective it means excellent or splendid, so fine in the approving sense.

clue.text: Duck managed to eviscerate an Asian animal

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so the letter O
to run something is to manage it; ran is the past tense
to gut is to remove the innards

explanation.surface: A duck succeeded in disembowelling an animal from Asia, a grisly scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The great red ape lives only in Borneo and Sumatra, so it is an Asian animal.

clue.text: Very great depth in one, a nation of old

parts.note: an abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A deep chasm within one ancient country.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the former name of Ethiopia, so a country of the past.

clue.text: Cross noted?

definitions.meaning: cross here means irritable or bad-tempered
read playfully as full of crotchets, quarter-note marks in written music

explanation.surface: A query whether someone was known to be angry.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: a crotchet is the British name for a quarter note, so music full of them could be called noted in this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumpy and irritable is the dictionary sense, a plain synonym for cross.

clue.text: Always busy, he got on badly

indicators.note: badly means poorly done, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who never stops, but did poorly at it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone constantly active and on the move, never resting.

clue.text: What politician may do with coarse material on son

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed after the cloth

parts.note: canvas is a heavy, coarse woven cloth
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A rough fabric worn by a politician's son, perhaps on the campaign trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Going door to door seeking votes before an election is what a politician may do.

clue.text: Cram facts

definitions.meaning: to cram is to pack something full
informal for material or information, as in knowing your subject matter

explanation.surface: An instruction to a student to swot up on facts.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means pack tightly; as a noun it means material, here information or knowledge.

clue.text: Arm photographer?

definitions.meaning: an arm is a weapon, here a gun
a cameraman shoots pictures, so is jokingly named after that verb

explanation.surface: A query about equipping a cameraman.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a gun is a weapon or arm, and one who shoots film or photos is a photographer.

clue.text: Staff after cakes removing lid, so open

indicators.note: after puts the staff word at the end
removing the lid takes off the top letter, the first in a down answer

parts.note: buns are small sweet cakes
a crew is the staff of a ship or aircraft

explanation.surface: Staff, after eating cakes, take the lid off something to open it.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn a cap or lid until it comes off is a way to open a container.

clue.text: Fiendish setters always take assumed names in crosswords, initially

indicators.note: initially says the first letter of each of the preceding words is taken

explanation.surface: A wry claim that crossword setters are devilish for always using pseudonyms.
explanation.walkthrough: Telegraph setters do often appear under pen-names, which makes the surface ring true.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilish or wicked, like the devil himself, is what fiendish means.

clue.text: The mating game?

parts.note: playfully, a board game that ends in checkmate is a game about mating

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests courtship; mate here is the winning move in a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The board game of kings and queens is won by checkmate, so it is literally a mating game.

clue.text: Spoons bent right back

indicators.note: bent means twisted out of shape, so the letters of the word before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone bends spoons right back, like a party-trick performer.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or event financially is to support them with money, the verb's synonym.

clue.text: Work over, repeat in error

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

indicators.note: in error means mistakenly, so the word's letters are set down wrongly

explanation.surface: An instruction to rework a job, warning against repeating a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Machines are said to function or run, a verb sense matching work.

clue.text: Ebbing brown river, pure

indicators.note: ebbing means flowing back, so the colour word is read in reverse

parts.note: tan is a light brown colour
the Ural is a river flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: A brown river flowing back out, its water clean and unspoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadulterated, with nothing added, is a sense shared with pure, as in natural yoghurt.

clue.text: Flier spouse distributed in school

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters go inside the school name

parts.note: Harrow is a famous English public school in north-west London

indicators.note: distributed means spread around, so the word's letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A pilot whose husband or wife is spread about a school, an odd picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A common small brown bird is a flier, the setter's playful name for anything with wings.
